goals.why_it_matters: This pillar owns the one surface outsiders can see, and it is the surface that goes stale fastest. The page still promises 'no menus to learn and no words to read' — which is a claim about phase 1's farming loop (S-7 binds the core loop, and only phase 1), made about a whole game whose later phases run to programmable bots and will need words by design. The build growing text is the design working; the copy not keeping up is the failure, and it is ours.

goals.statement: A child who cannot read can still play the farming loop.
goals.statement_short: nobody is checking that the farming loop stays readable-free
goals.why_it_matters: S-7's actual promise, and the accessibility claim the store page is really making. The shop was deliberately stripped of words and builds itself from icons and numerals; the machine panel has words and is reached at 150g, days of farming away. Which surfaces a pre-reader must cross is the whole question, and it is a judgment about the game rather than a property of the source.

measure.reason: No grep can tell the shop apart from the machine panel — both are labels in ui/menus.gd, and whether one sits on the farming loop is a judgment about which surfaces a player has to cross to farm. A check counting every English string in the build would go redder with every phase, by design, which is the wrong shape of check entirely.
measure.would_need: A named list of the surfaces the farming loop crosses, so a check can scan those and ignore the rest — which is a design ruling before it is a checker.

path_to_green.narrative: Name the surfaces the farming loop crosses. Then this becomes a real check instead of a promise nobody tests.

action.ask: S-7 says phase 1's core loop needs no reading, but nothing lists which surfaces that covers. Walk the farming loop — clear, till, plant, water, sleep, harvest, buy seeds — and name every surface a player crosses to do it. That list turns an untested promise into a check, and it also settles the scope argument in the open robot-menu question: whether a machine panel is inside the loop or outside it.
